nodes.name: RuO2 molten salt synthesis
nodes.procedure: 5 g NaNO3 was initially heated at 400 °C for 30 min in an oven under air atmosphere, then 50 mg RuCl3 powder was poured into the molten NaNO3 and kept at 400 °C for 10 min. Afterwards, the cooled solid was washed by water 3 times to remove the NaNO3 and dried overnight to obtain the synthesized RuO2.

nodes.name: Pt doping and reduction
nodes.procedure: 50 mg synthesized RuO2 was dispersed in 18 ml water and 7 mg PtCl4 dissolved in 2 mL water was dropwise added into the above solution under continuously stirring. After the formation of a homogeneous mixture, it was heated to 90 °C and kept stirring for 16 h. Finally, the Pt species absorbed RuO2 was washed by water for 3 times and collected by centrifugation, followed by calcination in Ar at 450 °C for 2 h with a heating rate of 5 °C min−1 to obtain the Pt-Ru/RuO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows flat-spread and dense nanostructure of Pt-Ru/RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1a, the flat-spread and dense nanostructure of Pt-Ru/RuO2 was initially characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows Ru (101) lattice spacing of 2.07 Å and RuO2 (110) lattice spacing of 3.18 Å with evident grain boundaries.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A typical high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image indicates that the Pt-Ru/RuO2 consists of independently distributed crystal regions belong to Ru and RuO2, with evident grain boundaries among them.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC HAADF-STEM visualizes isolated Pt single atoms homogeneously dispersed on both Ru and RuO2 regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As revealed in Fig. 1c, d, two distinct crystal regions... the isolated bright spots correspond to Pt atoms are directly visualized and homogenously dispersed on both Ru and RuO2 regions.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms coexistence of Ru (JCPDS No. 06-0663) and RuO2 (JCPDS No. 43-1027) phases; Rietveld refinement gives Ru molar ratio of 25.18% in Pt-Ru/RuO2 and 15.03% in Ru/RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To reveal the detailed crystal structures of Pt-Ru/RuO2 and Ru/RuO2, X-ray diffraction (XRD) was employed... the Ru molar ratio is calculated to be 15.03% in Ru/RuO2, and a slightly more Ru (25.18%) appears on Pt-Ru/RuO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDS confirms Pt atomic ratio of 1.36% in Pt-Ru/RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM-EDS and ICP-OES determine that the atomic ratio of Pt is 1.36% in Pt-Ru/RuO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirms Pt atomic ratio of 1.36% in Pt-Ru/RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM-EDS and ICP-OES determine that the atomic ratio of Pt is 1.36% in Pt-Ru/RuO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ru 3p shows Ru0/Ru4+ ratio increasing from 0.16 in Ru/RuO2 to 0.28 in Pt-Ru/RuO2; O 1s peaks at 529.3 eV (lattice O), 530.9 eV (absorbed OH-/O2), 532.5 eV (absorbed H2O); Pt 4f shows metallic Pt (single-atom alloy in Ru region) and oxidized Pt (coordinated by O on RuO2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: both Ru 3p XPS spectra on Pt-Ru/RuO2 and Ru/RuO2 can be deconvoluted into doublets of Ru0 and Ru4+, implying the coexistence of metallic Ru and RuO2. After the introduction of Pt, the ratio of Ru0/Ru4+ is increased from 0.16 to 0.28... Supplementary Fig. 8c shows the O 1s spectra... Pt 4f XPS spectrum indicates that... both metallic Pt and oxidized Pt are found on Pt-Ru/RuO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES white-line position between Pt foil and PtO2 indicates oxidized Pt state between 0 and +4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Fig. 1g, the white-line energy position of Pt-Ru/RuO2 is located between Pt foil and PtO2, implying the oxidized state of Pt species is between 0 and +4.

properties.description: X-ray Absorption Near Edge Structure spectrum

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge EXAFS shows Pt-O at 1.67 Å (main), Pt-Ru at 2.59 Å, Pt-O-Ru at 3.29 Å; no Pt-Pt bond detected; WT-EXAFS maximum at R=1.53 Å, k=4.90 Å⁻¹ confirms Pt-O scattering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt-Ru/RuO2 exhibits a dominant peak at 1.67 Å in the R-space... corresponding to Pt-O bond. Additionally, no discernible peak related to Pt–Pt bond... model-based EXAFS fit... main peak located at 1.67 Å is Pt–O bond, other peaks at 2.59 Å and 3.29 Å are derived from Pt–Ru and Pt–O–Ru moieties.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows average oxidation states of +2.8 for Pt-Ru/RuO2 and +3.3 for Ru/RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through establishing the standard curves... the average oxidation states of Ru on Pt-Ru/RuO2 and Ru/RuO2 are determined as +2.8 and +3.3, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS shows peaks identical to RuO2 plus subtle Ru-Ru bond at 2.30 Å, confirming presence of reduced Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: both the Ru K-edge EXAFS spectra of Pt-Ru/RuO2 and Ru/RuO2 show the identical peaks as RuO2 except the subtle peaks attributed to Ru–Ru bond present at 2.30 Å.
